title: Graceful API-version bridge: phased behavior flags, replay harness, and structured-output validation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We need a low-risk path to evolve the Core API streaming semantics, tool/function calling wire format, and structured-output wiring without breaking existing clients. Previous migrations have exposed regressions when streaming chunk boundaries and toolcall event ordering changed, and customers have strict contracts for structured JSON outputs.

Goal: Deliver a runtime-side compatibility bridge and a test harness that lets us progressively enable new behavior flags per-customer and measure for regressions in correctness, latency, and cost. Provide a documented migration guide for SDKs and operators and a canary rollout plan with clear rollback signals.

Scope:
- Runtime middleware that can translate between legacy streaming frames and the new framed-toolcall protocol.
- Behavior flags: use_streaming_v2, toolcall_strict_order, structured_output_strict_parsing. Flags must be configurable per-tenant and per-route.
- Replay harness to run requests against both old and new code paths (shadowing & differential assertions).
- Golden prompt sets and automated validation for structured outputs (schema conformance + fuzzed partial-chunk scenarios).
- Canary rollout orchestration (console + infra hooks) and rollback criteria tied to token-diff thresholds, error rates, and customer-reported regressions.

Non-goals: full SDK migrations (SDK teams will consume the migration guide and client flags); changing model semantics themselves (this is a serving compatibility layer).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime bridge implements translation for legacy chunked events and new framed toolcall messages with <1ms median added latency in isolation
Per-tenant behavior flags can be toggled via control plane and respected by serving nodes within 30s
Replay harness can execute 10k recorded sessions/day and produce token-level diffs, structured-output schema mismatches, and timing deltas
Migration guide published with step-by-step SDK examples and recommended client wave sizes
Canary rollouts include automated rollback triggers: >0.5% new error spike OR >2% structured-output schema mismatch OR customer-reported regression from opt-in canary group
milestones: Design review and API surface proposal (2026-02-26)
Full rollout gating and post-rollout audit (2026-03-29)
implementation_notes:
Spike findings: two translation modes are cheaper than trying to normalize at the source. Mode A does on-the-fly framing for streaming-only changes; Mode B applies a toolcall reorder buffer when legacy interleaving could break tool invocation ordering. Mode selection is automated based on route metadata. We measure added p95 latency of 5-8ms when under load for Mode B; further kernel tuning in runtime-2.4 expected to cut this.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Doing translation in the proxy vs in the runtime: runtime keeps visibility into KV cache and batching so we opted for runtime bridge despite slightly higher surface area.
- Strict structured parsing may reject fuzzed outputs from older models; we will provide a permissive-to-strict migration path and automatic enrichment heuristics to reduce false positives.

Open questions:
- What are acceptable token-diff thresholds for hallucination/regression across customers? (PM to sign off)
- Do we expose flag toggles to self-serve console or hide behind support for enterprise-only waves?
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for frame translation and reorder buffer (coverage target 95%)
Integration suite simulating partial-chunk delivery and reconnect events
Shadow replay: run historical traffic against new path and produce daily regression reports
End-to-end structured-output validator using JSON schemas + property-based fuzzing
Load test matrix comparing baseline vs bridge under realistic batching profiles
canary_plan: Stage 1: internal teams + engineering-owned tenants (1% traffic) — 72h monitoring
Stage 2: opt-in customers + selected PLG cohorts (10% traffic) — 5 day monitoring
Stage 3: gradual ramp to 50% with pause points and automated rollback checks
All stages emit token-diff histograms, error traces, and per-tenant structured-output mismatch dashboards
rollback_criteria: >0.5% increase in 5xx errors attributed to bridge path
>3x baseline increase in structured-output schema mismatches for any customer
Latency p95 increase >20% for an SLA-bound tenant
Escalation: a verified customer-reported blocking regression
